question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose safety-event emission and subscription as a public plugin SDK contract backed by shared durable history, or should the initial implementation remain a narrower core-owned diagnostics surface?
rationale: This determines external compatibility, cross-plugin data access, retention obligations, and the correct owner boundary; it cannot be safely selected by a mechanical patch repair.

options.title: Approve a narrow core contract
options.body: Define the stable event schema, subscriber authorization, retention policy, and migration guarantees before continuing with the plugin and UI surfaces.

options.title: Keep it core-internal initially
options.body: Land only a reviewed internal diagnostics seam and defer public plugin emission/subscription until maintainers approve a versioned SDK contract.

options.title: Route optional integrations outward
options.body: Keep core diagnostics generic and move plugin-specific safety dashboards or exporters to separately maintained plugins once a minimal seam exists.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define the stable event schema, subscriber authorization, retention policy, and migration guarantees before continuing with the plugin and UI surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The implementation and linked feature proposal are part of the same proposal series, though this is only a low-confidence routing signal rather than an ownership determination.
